newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Friday were inactive following sales this week that eventually pulled prices to $67.00 per cwt, down $2.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
There were a few light bids early at $67.00 that were passed by owners asking mostly $68.00, with a few at $69.00.
Most showlists reportedly will have carryover into next week, but many of the cattle not sold were unfinished and could use the extra days on feed, they said.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by slipping beef prices following hefty beef production last week, they said.

Uncertainty over Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report also was in the market, with several feedlot managers saying estimates for large on-feed supplies as of May and active placements during April were too big.

Analysts' pre-report estimates for on-feed supplies averaged 109.6 percent of a year ago from a range of 108.0 to 111.0. April placement estimates averaged 113.9 percent from a range of 104.9 to 127.5 and April marketings averaged 101.0 percent from 98.6 to 104.0.
